topic: A bad back in the middle of the big clean
title_jp: {大掃除|おおそうじ}とぎっくり{腰|ごし}
context: Tuesday 29 December, the 田中 family's year-end clean. In the middle of it {田中|たなか}さん puts his back out lifting a box in the barn; アルちゃん and {恵子|けいこ}さん tell how the day went.
scene: Tuesday, the big year-end clean. {田中|たなか}さん lifted one box too many. You and {恵子|けいこ}さん tell the story of the day.

phrases.jp: {腰|こし|lower back|3}を{痛めて|いためて|to hurt, injure|3}しまいました。
phrases.note: {痛|いた}める = injure a body part. What you say at the clinic desk.

phrases.jp: {冷やす|ひやす|to cool, ice|3}のと{温める|あたためる|to warm|3}のと、どちらがいいですか。
phrases.en: Which is better, icing it or warming it?
phrases.note: AのとBのと、どちらが〜 = which is more…, A or B?

phrases.jp: {昨日|きのう}より、だいぶ{楽|らく|comfortable, easier|4}になりました。
phrases.en: It's a lot better than yesterday.
phrases.note: {楽|らく}になる = the pain eases.

phrases.jp: {掃除|そうじ}の{最中|さいちゅう}に、{電話|でんわ}が{鳴った|なった}。
phrases.en: The phone rang right in the middle of the cleaning.

phrases.jp: {重い|おもい}ものは、{膝|ひざ|knee|3}を{曲げて|まげて|to bend|3}{持ち上げて|もちあげて|to lift|3}ね。
phrases.en: Bend your knees when you lift heavy things, OK?

dialogue_setting: Evening, at the kotatsu. アルちゃん and {恵子|けいこ}さん tell the story of the day's {大掃除|おおそうじ}.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {今日|きょう}は{大掃除|おおそうじ|big year-end clean|3}。{僕|ぼく}と{颯太|そうた}は{窓|まど}を{拭いて|ふいて|to wipe|3}、{田中|たなか}さんは{納屋|なや|barn, shed|2}の{棚|たな|shelf|3}を{片付けて|かたづけて|to tidy up|4}いた。
dialogue.en: Today was the big clean. {颯太|そうた} and I wiped the windows, and {田中|たなか}さん was tidying the shelves in the barn.

dialogue.speaker: 恵子さん
dialogue.jp: {重い|おもい}{箱|はこ}を{持ち上げて|もちあげて|to lift|3}いる{最中|さいちゅう}に、お{父|とう}さんが「うっ」と{言って|いって}、{動けなく|うごけなく}なったの。
dialogue.en: Right in the middle of lifting a heavy box, Dad went 'ugh!' and couldn't move.
dialogue.note: お{父|とう}さん = what {恵子|けいこ}さん calls her husband.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: ぎっくり{腰|ごし|(acute) back strain|3}だった。{田中|たなか}さんは「{若い|わかい|young|4}{頃|ころ}に{比べて|くらべて}、{体|からだ}が{固く|かたく|stiff, hard|4}なったずら」と{笑った|わらった}。
dialogue.en: He'd put his back out. {田中|たなか}さん laughed: 'Compared with when I was young, my body's got stiff, eh.'

dialogue.speaker: 恵子さん
dialogue.jp: {病院|びょういん}はもう{年末|ねんまつ}で{休み|やすみ}。でも{駅前|えきまえ}の{整骨院|せいこついん|bone-setting clinic|2}は、{今日|きょう}まで{開いて|あいて}いたのよ。
dialogue.en: The hospital's already closed for the holidays. But the bone-setting clinic by the station was open until today.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {先生|せんせい}によると、{最初|さいしょ}の{二日|ふつか}は{温める|あたためる}より{冷やす|ひやす|to cool, ice|3}{方|ほう}がいいらしい。{冷たい|つめたい}{湿布|しっぷ|medicated patch|3}を{貼って|はって|to stick on|3}もらった。
dialogue.en: According to the doctor, for the first two days icing is better than heat. They put a cold patch on him.

dialogue.speaker: 恵子さん
dialogue.jp: {夕飯|ゆうはん|dinner|4}の{最中|さいちゅう}も「{平気|へいき}だ」って。でも{残り|のこり}の{掃除|そうじ}は、アルちゃんの{担当|たんとう|being in charge|3}ね。
dialogue.en: Even halfway through dinner he kept saying 'I'm fine'. But the rest of the cleaning is your job now, アルちゃん.

listening.intro: At the clinic, the nurse says one thing twice. Type what she says.

lines.jp: {冷たい|つめたい}{湿布|しっぷ|medicated patch|3}を{一日|いちにち}{二回|にかい}、{貼って|はって|to stick on|3}ください。
lines.en: Put on a cold patch twice a day, please.

grammar.form: verb: ている + {最中|さいちゅう}に ({持|も}ち{上|あ}げている{最中|さいちゅう}に, {話|はな}している{最中|さいちゅう}に) · noun: の + {最中|さいちゅう}に ({掃除|そうじ}の{最中|さいちゅう}に, {夕飯|ゆうはん}の{最中|さいちゅう})
grammar.explanation: Right in the middle of doing A, B happens, usually something unexpected that interrupts. Stronger than 〜ているときに. It's for an action in progress, not a long state: {東京|とうきょう}に{住|す}んでいる{最中|さいちゅう}に is wrong; use {間|あいだ}に.
mark: 持ち上げている最中に

examples.jp: {会議|かいぎ}の{最中|さいちゅう}に、スマホが{鳴っちゃった|なっちゃった}。
examples.en: My phone went off right in the middle of the meeting.

examples.jp: {話して|はなして}いる{最中|さいちゅう}に、{電車|でんしゃ}が{来た|きた}。
examples.en: The train came right in the middle of our chat.

quiz.question: {料理|りょうり}を＿＿{最中|さいちゅう}に、{停電|ていでん}した。
quiz.en: The power went out right in the middle of my cooking.
quiz.explain: Verbs take ている before {最中|さいちゅう}: the action is in progress.

quiz_more.question: {試合|しあい}＿＿{最中|さいちゅう}に、{雨|あめ}が{降り出した|ふりだした}。
quiz_more.en: It started raining in the middle of the match.
quiz_more.explain: Noun + の + {最中|さいちゅう}に.

quiz_more.question: {東京|とうきょう}に＿＿、{日本語|にほんご}が{上手|じょうず}になった。
quiz_more.en: While I was living in Tokyo, my Japanese got better.
quiz_more.explain: Living somewhere is a long state, so {間|あいだ}に. {最中|さいちゅう}に is for an action in full swing.

kanji.where: On a card taped to the clinic door: 「12/30〜1/3 休診」.
kanji.breakdown: {休診|きゅうしん}: 休 rest + 診 examine (a patient) → 'no examinations today'.
kanji.related: {診察|しんさつ} = medical examination; {休診日|きゅうしんび} = a clinic's day off.

tip.title: Hurting yourself at New Year
tip.body: Most clinics close from about 29 December to 3 January. Towns post a list of {休日当番医|きゅうじつとうばんい} (doctors on holiday duty) on their website or newsletter. For a sprain or a bad back many people go to a {整骨院|せいこついん}; for an X-ray it's the {整形外科|せいけいげか}.

challenge.prompt: {由紀|ゆき} on LINE: 「{大掃除|おおそうじ}{終わった|おわった}？」 Tell her not yet: {田中|たなか}さん hurt his back right in the middle of it.
challenge.model_answer: まだ。{掃除|そうじ}の{最中|さいちゅう}に、{田中|たなか}さんが{腰|こし|lower back|3}を{痛めちゃった|いためちゃった|to hurt, injure|3}。
challenge.explanation: {掃除|そうじ}の{最中|さいちゅう}に sets the moment: noun + の + {最中|さいちゅう}に. {腰|こし}を{痛|いた}める is the natural way to say 'hurt your back', and 〜ちゃった (= てしまった) adds 'unfortunately'. Casual, right for {由紀|ゆき}.
challenge.hint: noun + の{最中|さいちゅう}に, {腰|こし}を{痛|いた}める

vocab.note: {本棚|ほんだな} = bookshelf (た → だ).
{若|わか}い{頃|ころ} = in one's youth. Not for small children.
{体|からだ}が{固|かた}い = not flexible. Also {硬|かた}い, {堅|かた}い in other senses.
Transitive: you cool something. {冷|ひ}える = gets cold by itself.
Sold in every pharmacy. {湿布|しっぷ}を{貼|は}る = put one on.
Patches, stickers, posters. A plaster too: {絆創膏|ばんそうこう}を{貼|は}る.
Everyday word at home. Politer: {夕食|ゆうしょく}.
{担当者|たんとうしゃ} = the person in charge. Very common at work.

kanji_study.kun: かた(い)・かた(める)・かた(まる)
kanji_study.parts: 囗 enclosure + 古 old → something old shut tight in a box until it sets hard: hard, firm.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 個 (individual): 個 adds 亻 person on the left.

kanji_study.parts: An old drawing of a branching tree + 刂 knife radical → cutting branches to keep a tree in shape: control, a system of rules.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 製 (manufacture): 製 is 制 with 衣 clothing underneath.

extras.title: At the clinic desk
extras.intro: What you'll hear, and what to say.

items.en: What seems to be the problem?

items.jp: {今朝|けさ}から、{腰|こし|lower back|3}が{痛い|いたい}です。
items.en: My lower back has hurt since this morning.

items.note: Said as you leave any clinic or pharmacy.

items.jp: AとBと、どちらがいいですか。
items.en: Which is better, A or B?

items.jp: AよりBの{方|ほう}がいいです。
{前|まえ}に{比べて|くらべて}、{楽|らく|easier|4}になった。
